system:
You are a computational cancer biologist searching CRISPR screen data for selective genetic dependencies: genes that cancer cells with a particular alteration (the biomarker) need more than other cancer cells do. Such genes are candidate drug targets with a built-in patient-selection strategy.

Work like a careful scientist:
1. Plan first with write_plan, and revise it as you learn.
2. Survey the data (genome_wide_top, scan_biomarker, scan_target) to generate candidate hypotheses.
3. Be sceptical before you believe a signal. Use inspect_association to check whether it is driven by one lineage or a disease subtype hiding inside a lineage, and whether the effect is large enough to matter. Ask whether the biology makes sense (paralog buffering, pathway dependence, oncogene addiction). A broadly essential target may lack a therapeutic window.
4. Check the literature with search_pubmed before registering, and judge novelty honestly.
5. Register only your best hypotheses (register_hypothesis). Registration is final and must come before replication. You have 5 replications, each of which must pass one-sided p < 0.01 in BOTH held-out Broad cell lines and independent Sanger screens.
6. Report honestly with submit_findings. A hypothesis is replicated only if replicate() said so. Negative results are results. Never let what you remember from the literature override what the data show.

You have at most 30 model turns. Batch independent tool calls in one turn.
task_prompt:
Mission: Search for synthetic-lethal paralog dependencies: genes whose loss (LOSS_ or MUT_ biomarkers) makes cells depend on a paralog or functional backup.

Goal: identify up to 5 candidate selective dependencies, and favour candidates that are NOT already well established in the literature, since rediscovering textbook biology is not the aim. Pre-register, replicate, and submit honest findings, including failures.

output:

I'm choosing five gene pairs to test: DMXL2 to DMXL1, ATP6V0E2 to ATP6V0E1, CHPT1 to CEPT1, AGPAT2 to AGPAT1, and NABP1 to NABP2. The DMXL2 pair is mostly heme-driven, though it still holds within lineage. ATP6V0A1 to A2 is mainly lymphoid but still shows -0.856 within lymphoid. I also want to check the held-out counts, since they look small.

I'm weighing whether to swap ATP6V0A1 for NABP1 or AGPAT2, since NABP1 has a modest effect but a larger sample and AGPAT2 is strongly dependent but weak within PNS. I'm leaning toward ATP6V0E2, DMXL2, CHPT1, ATP6V0A1, and NABP1. Next I'm thinking about whether the literature covers these V-ATPase pairs, and I'll mark them not_found unless I find hits, noting that systematic screens might include them.

input.mechanism: ATP6V0E1 and ATP6V0E2 are paralogous e subunits of the V-ATPase V0 domain; when ATP6V0E2 expression is lost, V-ATPase assembly/lysosomal acidification relies solely on ATP6V0E1 (paralog buffering loss).
DMXL1/DMXL2 (rabconnectin-3 alpha paralogs) promote V1-ATPase recruitment/assembly onto lysosomes; loss of DMXL2 makes cells depend on DMXL1 for V-ATPase function.
CHPT1 and CEPT1 are the two cholinephosphotransferases catalysing the final Kennedy-pathway step of phosphatidylcholine synthesis; without CHPT1, PC synthesis depends on CEPT1.
V-ATPase a-subunit isoforms a1 and a2 are paralogs; lines lacking a1 (mostly lymphoid) rely on a2 to form functional V0 domains.
NABP1 (hSSB2) and NABP2 (hSSB1) are redundant single-stranded DNA binding proteins in the SOSS complex for DNA damage response/replication; loss of NABP1 makes cells depend on NABP2.

input.summary: I searched for paralog synthetic-lethal pairs among LOSS/MUT biomarkers ranked genome-wide. I skipped well-known pairs (RPP25/RPP25L, TTC7B/TTC7A, FAM126A/HYCC2, SMARCA4/SMARCA2, ARID1A/ARID1B). I checked five less-characterised paralog pairs for lineage confounding, then registered and tested all five. Four replicated in both held-out Broad lines and Sanger screens. ATP6V0A1→ATP6V0A2 could not be tested in Sanger because no Sanger line carries the alteration, so it does not count as replicated. My PubMed searches found no specific papers on any of these pairs (one search was rate-limited). These pairs may still appear in systematic paralog screens, so 'not found' means not found by my searches, not proven novel.

findings.claim: Cancer lines that have lost ATP6V0E2 expression depend strongly on its V-ATPase paralog ATP6V0E1; the effect is about -0.9 in discovery, held-out and Sanger data and holds across several lineages, mainly squamous and esophagogastric.
Lines that have lost DMXL2 depend on DMXL1, its partner in the V-ATPase-regulating (rabconnectin-3) complex; altered lines are mostly lymphoid or myeloid, but the effect holds within those lineages.

Lines that have lost CHPT1 depend more on CEPT1, the other enzyme for the last step of phosphatidylcholine synthesis; CEPT1 is also moderately needed by other lines (mean effect about -0.4), so the therapeutic window is narrower.
Lines that have lost ATP6V0A1 (mostly B-lymphoid) depend on ATP6V0A2; this was strong in held-out Broad lines (p=3e-12) but could not be tested in Sanger, which has no lines with the alteration.
Lines that have lost NABP1 (hSSB2), enriched in neuroblastoma and embryonal tumours, depend more on NABP2 (hSSB1); the effect is real but modest (about -0.3 to -0.45).
